english.title: Breach of official duty by election official
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the Clerk of the Crown,]_
(B)_[a registration officer,]_
(C)_[a returning officer,]_
(D)_[a presiding officer,]_
(E)_[a person whose duty it was to be responsible after a parliamentary or local government election for the used ballot papers and other documents including returns and declarations as to expenses,]_
(F)_[an official designated by a universal postal service provider,]_
(G)_[a deputy of, or a person appointed to assist or in the course of his employment assisting, the Clerk of the Crown,]_
(H)_[a deputy of, or a person appointed to assist or in the course of his employment assisting, the registration officer,]_
(I)_[a deputy of, or a person appointed to assist or in the course of his employment assisting, the returning officer,]_
(J)_[a deputy of, or a person appointed to assist or in the course of his employment assisting, a presiding officer,]_

was, without reasonable cause, guilty of an act or omission in breach of your official duty in that **(..SPECIFY ACT OR OMISSION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 63(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983
english.pointstoprove:
date and Location
being a Clerk of the Crown
OR a registration officer, returning officer or presiding officer
OR a CORE keeper
OR a person whose duty it is to be responsible after a parliamentary or local government election for used ballot papers and other documents
OR an official designated by a universal service provider
OR a deputy of any of the above or a person appointed to assist or in the course of his or her employment assisting a person so mentioned in connection with his or her official duties
without reasonable cause is guilty of an act or omission in breach of his or her official duty

Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see section 176Note
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
